name: Leucetius

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Leucetius is a Continental Celtic and British god. Few inscriptions in Gaul and Britain name him. He is the consort of Nemetona, the goddess of sacred groves. An inscription to the pair was found at the healing shrine of Bath, which the Romans called Aquae Sulis. That find marks Leucetius as a healing god. In Gaul the Celts took him as a form of the war god Mars. His name holds the syllable for bright and may mean lightning.

okr.objective: Record the obscure healing god Leucetius from the found inscriptions.
